content.text:
Build and run a complete backup crawler for https://medpsycmoss.com/

CRITICAL CONTEXT: This site is built on the HostGator "Gator" website builder and is
CLIENT-SIDE RENDERED — the raw HTML from the server contains only the footer; all page
content is painted by JavaScript. A plain wget/requests mirror will capture empty shells.
You MUST render every page in a headless browser (Playwright) before saving anything.

GOAL: A complete local backup so the client's site can be fully reconstructed if needed.
We are about to migrate this site to a new platform; this backup runs BEFORE any changes.

REQUIREMENTS:

1. Python 3 + Playwright (chromium). Create a venv, install deps, run `playwright
   install chromium` yourself.

2. Seed the crawl with these known URLs, then BFS-crawl every same-domain link
   discovered on rendered pages (cap: 300 pages):
   /, /about, /about-me, /store, /podcast, /blog, /contact, /events, /my-work,
   /interviews, /vlogs, /trauma-resources, /websites-for-trauma, /resources,
   /pelvic-pain-resources, /products/residency-personal-statement,
   /products/mock-interviews, /products/loa-guide, /products/usmle-accommodations,
   /residency-app, /failure-identity, /clinical-rotations
   Also fetch /sitemap.xml and /robots.txt if they exist and add any sitemap URLs
   to the queue.

3. For every page (wait for networkidle + ~1.5s settle):
   a. Save the fully rendered DOM to backup/pages/<slug>.html
   b. Save a full-page screenshot to backup/screenshots/<slug>.png
   c. Extract readable content (title, headings, paragraphs, image URLs, link map)
      into backup/content/<slug>.md — clean markdown, this doubles as the content
      source for the rebuild.

4. Register a network response listener BEFORE navigation and save EVERY asset
   response (content-types: image/*, css, javascript, font/*, pdf, audio/*, video/*)
   into backup/assets/<host>/<path>, mirroring URL structure. Include third-party
   CDN hosts — Gator serves media from CDN domains, not from medpsycmoss.com.
   Deduplicate by URL. Skip non-200s.

5. Store pages matter most: make sure every /store and /products/* page is captured
   including product titles, descriptions, and prices in the markdown extraction.

6. Robustness: one failing page or asset must never kill the crawl — log to
   backup/errors.log and continue. 1 page at a time, no parallel hammering,
   small delay between pages (be polite, it's a client's live site).

7. Write backup/manifest.txt listing every page + asset saved, with counts.

8. VERIFY the backup before declaring success: programmatically check that at
   least 15 saved HTML files contain >2000 characters of body text (proves JS
   rendering worked, not footer-only shells), that screenshots exist and are
   >50KB, and that image assets were captured. Print a verification report.

9. When verification passes, zip the backup/ folder to
   medpsycmoss-backup-<YYYYMMDD>.zip and print the final summary.

Run the whole thing end-to-end and show me the verification report and any URLs
that failed.

    say("  RESULT: %s" % ("PASS" if check5 else "FAIL"))

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- summary
    checks = [
        ("JS rendering (>=15 pages >2000 chars)", check1),
        ("screenshots present and >50KB", check2),
        ("assets incl. images captured", check3),
        ("markdown extraction complete", check4),
